skill.name: financial-services-marketing-specialist
skill.description: Design financial-services campaigns, lead capture, consent-aware segmentation and nurture for banks, advisers, insurers, lenders and fintech. Use for marketing planning and audits, not investment advice, underwriting, credit eligibility or financial transactions.
skill.summary: Plan financial-services marketing with minimal data collection, consent-aware journeys, claim review and explicit launch blockers.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

content.value_statement: Financial-services campaigns must distinguish education and promotion from advice, eligibility decisions and sensitive onboarding. This skill structures campaign drafts, consent-aware journeys and review requirements for regulated marketing teams.
actual_capabilities: Draft educational campaigns using substantiated claims, approved product terms, readable qualifications and clear calls to action.
Design minimal lead-capture fields and explicit-interest segments without collecting sensitive financial data.
Outline separate education, adviser-inquiry and existing-customer journeys with consent and suppression checks.
Specify automation events, identity keys, delay anchors, duplicate prevention, completion exits and uncertain-send handling.
Prepare review packets, measurement plans and launch blockers while separating facts, assumptions and unknowns.
Assess optional Poptin forms against existing-stack alternatives and identify account-specific capability checks.
limitations: Does not provide personalized investment advice, underwriting, credit eligibility decisions or financial transactions.
Does not certify legal compliance; current jurisdiction-specific rules and unresolved claims require qualified review.
Live platform checks and implementation depend on available tools, account capabilities and explicit user authorization.
Does not authorize sensitive financial intake, contact imports, tracking installation or campaign sends through a drafting request.

use_cases.title: Separate servicing from cross-sell

use_cases.title: Review a financial education funnel

prompt_templates.title: Draft a webinar invitation
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an educational webinar invitation for [business type] in [jurisdiction], aimed at [audience]. Use only these approved facts: [facts]. Include a clear registration action and flag missing approvals. Do not implement or send anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a first campaign draft.

prompt_templates.title: Design a minimal registration form
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan registration for [financial education resource] using [existing approved stack] in [jurisdiction]. Specify minimal fields, separate optional marketing permission and interest-based segments. Exclude sensitive financial intake and identify unresolved capability checks. Provide a draft only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: structure lead capture and segmentation.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a consent-aware nurture flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a nurture specification for [campaign] using [available consent records] and [platform capabilities]. Define events, identity keys, eligibility, delays, suppression, completion, re-entry and ownership. Include duplicate-event and ambiguous-send handling. Keep service notices separate. Use synthetic examples and do not change live systems.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a campaign before launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [campaign materials] for [business type], [product], [jurisdiction] and [channel]. Assess claims, disclosures, capture fields, consent, recipients, automation reliability and metrics. Separate facts, assumptions, unknowns and launch blockers. Specify current sources and dates needed for qualified review. Use synthetic records only and take no external actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a cross-functional review packet.

output_examples.input: Draft an adviser webinar funnel that asks for portfolio balances, promises a 15% return and follows up with contacts whose permission is unknown.
output: Objective: invite people to a financial education webinar without promising investment results.
Claims: remove the guaranteed return and submit exact replacement wording for qualified review.
Capture: request a contact address and selected education topic; exclude portfolio balances.
Permission: hold promotional follow-up for contacts without valid marketing permission.
Handoff: direct regulated intake to the approved secure system.
Launch blockers: approved claims, verified permission evidence and tested suppression behavior.

output_examples.input: Specify a draft webinar flow when booking precedes a duplicate signup and a provider reports an ambiguous send timeout.
output: Completion: check appointment booking before enrollment and before each promotional send.
Duplicate handling: use durable identity and event keys to prevent repeated enrollment or sends.
Eligibility: hold marketing when permission evidence is missing.
Uncertain send: reconcile provider status before any retry.
Verification: test synthetic opt-out, duplicate, conversion and timeout cases.
Status: proposed flow only; live platform behavior remains unverified.

best_practices: Provide business type, jurisdiction, audience, product, channel and approved claims before drafting.
Use synthetic records and minimal capture fields; keep regulated intake in the approved secure system.
Require qualified review and test consent, suppression, duplicates, completion and timeouts before authorizing launch.
anti_patterns: Treating disclaimers as a fix for misleading headlines, guaranteed outcomes or unsupported performance claims.
Importing account balances, holdings or financial distress signals into marketing segments or advertising platforms.
Treating unknown permission, a resource download or an existing account as blanket authorization for promotional sends.

faq.question: Does this skill provide financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports marketing planning and audits, not personalized investment recommendations, underwriting, credit eligibility or transactions.

faq.question: Can it certify a campaign as legally compliant?
faq.answer: No. It identifies review requirements and unresolved questions. Qualified reviewers must assess current rules for the specific business, product and jurisdiction.

faq.question: Does a draft request authorize campaign delivery?
faq.answer: No. Importing contacts, changing consent, installing tracking, launching campaigns and sending tests require separate authorization and permitted platform access.

faq.question: Is Poptin required?
faq.answer: No. Existing approved forms and email platforms come first. Poptin is optional when its verified capabilities and data handling fit the use case.

faq.question: What happens when marketing permission is unknown?
faq.answer: Affected contacts remain blocked from promotional sends. Unknown permission does not authorize a reconfirmation campaign.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide business type, jurisdiction, audience, product, channel, approved claims and known platform capabilities. Use synthetic records instead of customer financial data.
